clue.text: Island soldier rejected a sort of owl soup

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the soldier's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the tawny owl is a common British owl

explanation.surface: A soldier from an island turns down a soup apparently made from owl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns GI round to IG.
explanation.definitionFit: Mulligatawny is a spicy curried broth of Anglo-Indian origin.

clue.text: Memorial stones for teachers

explanation.surface: Gravestones are put up for the teaching staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Markers are stones placed to mark a spot or grave; teachers mark pupils' work, so they are markers.

clue.text: King points to another tyro

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
N and E are points of the compass, north and east
another king, R being the abbreviation for rex

explanation.surface: A monarch gestures towards a fresh beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another king, the R of rex, after the first king, Lear; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a novice, someone still learning.

clue.text: -Is it weakness of -, birdie? I Cried" (Mikado)

definitions.text: Is it weakness of -, birdie? I Cried" (Mikado)

parts.words: Is it weakness of -, birdie? I Cried" (Mikado)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank line from Ko-Ko's song Tit-Willow in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, asking whether the bird's mind is failing

explanation.surface: A line quoted from a comic opera song addressed to a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Ko-Ko's song Tit-Willow in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado asks the bird whether its sorrow comes from weakness of mind or a tough worm inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means the mind or reasoning power, whose weakness Ko-Ko suspects in the bird.

clue.text: Range of some American destroyers

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A selection of US warships is lined up.
explanation.walkthrough: ANDES runs across 'AmericAN DEStroyers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the great mountain chain of South America, a range of peaks.

clue.text: Scotsman in real muddle dispensing charity

definitions.note: a phrase describing a person who gives alms, standing for that person

indicators.note: in means the Scotsman is placed inside the scrambled letters
muddle means the letters of real are jumbled

parts.note: mon is the Scots form of man

explanation.surface: A Scot in a real mess is handing out alms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddle' turns REAL into ALER, and 'in' puts MON inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was an official who distributed alms to the poor, or a hospital social worker.

clue.text: Girl and boy accepting eastern material

parts.note: Nan is a girl's name

indicators.note: accepting means the boy's name takes the eastern letter inside it

parts.note: Ken is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A couple welcome some fabric from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts E inside KEN to give KEEN; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanking in China.

clue.text: Pink confection — pre-Shakespeare, perhaps

parts.note: a sweet is a sugary confection
William comes before Shakespeare in the playwright's full name

explanation.surface: A pink candy, perhaps from before the Bard's time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink' looks like a colour; it is the flower family. 'pre-Shakespeare' is the name that comes before his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet william is a garden plant of the Dianthus genus, the pinks.

clue.text: A couple of kings in need of written authorization

indicators.note: in means the A and the kings are placed inside the word for need

parts.note: to need something is to want it
R (rex, Latin for king) twice gives two kings

explanation.surface: Two monarchs are short of a signed document permitting something.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrant is a document giving formal authority, as for an arrest or search.

clue.text: Having supernatural genius of French woman, almost

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: almost means the woman's name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Monica is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is said to have nearly uncanny brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last A of MONICA to leave MONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonic describes something possessed by or like a demon, a supernatural spirit or genius.

clue.text: Having correspondence with priest accepting people in orders

indicators.note: accepting means the priest's word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a curate is a junior clergyman

indicators.note: in means the people are put inside the orders

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, so OMS are orders
men are people

explanation.surface: Someone writes to a clergyman who is welcoming ordained folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MEN inside OMS to give OMMENS, and 'accepting' places that inside CURATE after its C; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Commensurate means corresponding in size or degree, so matching something proportionately.

clue.text: Unchanging EEC countries left outside

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed and scanned, 'Unchanging EEC countries left outside (7)', gives ETERNAL from 'Unchanging', but no reading of 'EEC countries left outside' builds ETERNAL; a search of the clue found nothing.

clue.text: Supplier of light timber introduced by young Dombey, say?

indicators.note: introduced by means the timber word follows the sound-alike word
say signals that the word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: in Dickens's Dombey and Son, young Paul Dombey is the son of the title
a beam is a length of timber

explanation.surface: A Dickens character brings in a delivery of wood that lets in light.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens's novel Dombey and Son gives SON for 'young Dombey'; 'say' makes it SUN, which 'introduced by' puts ahead of BEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a ray of sunshine, which brings brightness into a room.

clue.text: More discreet than the pussycat's spouse, for one

definitions.text: More discreet than the pussycat's spouse, for one

parts.words: More discreet than the pussycat's spouse, for one
parts.note: in Lear's poem The Owl and the Pussy-cat the pussycat marries the owl, the bird proverbially full of wisdom, so being more discreet than it means outdoing that wisdom

explanation.surface: Someone is more tactful than the husband in a nursery poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear's nonsense poem The Owl and the Pussy-cat ends with the two marrying; owls are proverbially wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Discreet means prudent and sensible, so more discreet is having more wisdom.

clue.text: Longevity of creed a nun modified

indicators.note: modified means the letters of creed, a and nun are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A nun's beliefs, adjusted, have lasted a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modified' rearranges CREED A NUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the power of lasting, which long life demonstrates.

clue.text: Lower your (and my) bearing

parts.note: to demean is to lower in dignity
our means belonging to you and me together

explanation.surface: Lower your posture, and mine too.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeanour is the way a person carries themselves, their outward manner.

clue.text: Function is to record a burst of mirth

parts.note: to log something is to record it

indicators.note: burst of means the letters of mirth are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone's job is to note down an outbreak of laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst of' rearranges MIRTH into RITHM.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a logarithm is a function, the inverse of raising to a power.

clue.text: Gradually understanding information to do with class

indicators.note: understanding read as under-standing: in this down answer the second piece stands beneath the first

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric, or Little by Little is a Victorian school story by F. W. Farrar, so Eric can stand for little by little

explanation.surface: Someone slowly grasps the facts about classification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understanding' says ERIC stands under GEN in the down grid. ERIC is a famous allusion: Farrar's school novel Eric, or Little by Little.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means relating to a whole genus or group, a category of things.

clue.text: Teachers in love nearly put up a building

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
in means the teachers go inside the shortened word for love
nearly means the last letter of the word for love is dropped

parts.note: to adore is to love
NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain

explanation.surface: Teachers, nearly in love, put up a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts ADORE to ADOR, 'in' puts NUT inside to give ADNUTOR, and 'put up' turns it all over. The NUT was Britain's National Union of Teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, often domed.

clue.text: They're bold, we hear, about introduction of slavery

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a dispute over money

indicators.note: introduction of means just the opening letter of slavery is used

explanation.surface: Brave people, it is said, discuss the beginning of the slave trade.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls delivered by the bowler, so overs are 'bowled', which sounds like 'bold'. 'we hear' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Overs in cricket are bowled, and bowled sounds like bold.

clue.text: Excel in public work

parts.note: overt means done openly, in public
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone shines in community service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise above or surpass, so outdo others.

clue.text: True, say, when broadcast by this big-mouth?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of true and say are strewn and reassembled

explanation.surface: A loudmouth's words are true, so to speak, when put on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big-mouth' suggests a boaster, but it is a river's wide mouth. 'when broadcast' rearranges TRUE SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An estuary is the wide tidal outlet where a river meets the sea.

clue.text: Fired for loose editing

indicators.note: loose means the letters of editing are set free to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lost their job because of sloppy editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests sacked, but here it means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ignited has been set on fire.

clue.text: A girl's company makes this entertainment

parts.note: Di's is the possessive of Di, a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman's firm puts on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is an evening of dancing to recorded music, a form of amusement.

clue.text: A comparatively good accomplice

parts.note: better is the comparative form of good

explanation.surface: A partner in crime is described as relatively decent.
explanation.definitionFit: An abetter helps or encourages another in wrongdoing, as an accomplice does.

clue.text: Troops have a right to be protected by explosive devices

indicators.note: to be protected by means the a and right go inside the word for the explosive devices

parts.note: mines are buried or floating explosive devices

explanation.surface: Soldiers are entitled to cover from bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: Marines are soldiers serving with a navy, so a body of fighting men.

clue.text: Have greater 14, being finally dismissed

parts.note: in cricket a batsman dismissed is out
last means finally, at the end

explanation.surface: Someone shows more stamina in being the last to be sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is ENDURANCE, so the definition reads 'have greater endurance'. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast a rival is to keep going longer than they do, showing more staying power.

clue.text: 24's singular kind of study

parts.note: 24 is MARINES; its singular gives marine, so this is the study of marine matters, the sea

explanation.surface: A particular branch of learning belongs to the troops of another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking 24 in the singular gives 'marine', read as the adjective for the sea, not a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanography is the science of the seas, which is marine study.
